summary: Build crisis messaging, media monitoring, and spokesperson response skills through practical simulations. Enrol in this five-day foundation course.
lede: Crisis media training prepares communications officers, spokespersons, and crisis coordinators to handle press engagement when facts are incomplete. It develops practical skills in classifying incidents, mapping messages, drafting holding statements, coordinating approvals, keeping enquiry logs, practising interviews, and assessing coverage and sentiment under time, evidence, and resource constraints.
audienceIntro: This foundation course is designed for professionals who prepare statements, handle journalist contact, support spokespersons, or coordinate crisis communication decisions. Media relations during crises training is especially relevant when you need a repeatable response process rather than relying on improvised messages.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: Basic experience writing workplace communications, handling stakeholder enquiries, or supporting organizational response activities. You should be able to interpret an incident brief and draft clear professional messages. Coding requirement: None. AI-assisted monitoring and media analytics are taught at conceptual awareness and operational application levels rather than technical engineering depth. Equipment: Bring a laptop capable of opening browser-based monitoring demonstrations and editable document templates.
